architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept realization-state control as adequate for progression if R <= 2.00, corresponding to a between-preparation spread no greater than 100%. This outcome falsifies none of H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; it only permits a subsequent matched-reference test.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity previously measured in the same chemistry family. It is measured directly across repeated preparations of the resin-modified AC1920+TK100 candidate, so it stays within support generated by this experiment and does not transfer the unmodified-family shared thermal-response shape. The result can establish formulation-level realization reproducibility, but cannot establish a molecular mechanism or, without a matched E2 reference, classify the registered relative-level hypotheses.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If R > 2.00, falsify the assumption that the current preparation protocol controls realization state to within the catalog's 100% state-control threshold. This outcome directly falsifies none of H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; instead, it prevents defensible adjudication of all three because preparation-state spread remains too large.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Repeat S1C41::M-REPEAT after tightening and fully recording dehydration, preparation, thermal history, residence time, and measurement order. Do not proceed to relative-level classification until the state-control criterion is met; after it is met, run S1C41::M-SWEEP with a contemporaneous matched E2 reference if such a matched-reference card becomes available.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Between-preparation viscosity-scale spread for at least three independent S1C41 preparations, quantified as R = exp(max(a_fr) - min(a_fr)), equivalently the maximum-to-minimum matched-temperature viscosity-scale ratio across the 80-130 C sweeps.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-REPEAT is admissible under the binding chemistry audit and directly resolves the dominant realization-state ambiguity before applying narrow level-classification thresholds. It cannot separate the three registered level hypotheses or test hot-hold drift, but it is the most scientifically defensible supplied card because the proposed one-sample sweep cannot attain its relative-to-E2 falsification criterion under the observed preparation variability.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator over the Proposer. The Proposer's S1C41::M-SWEEP is chemistry-admissible and top-ranked, but its single preparation and absent contemporaneous E2 reference cannot produce the stated relative-level observable reliably against the documented multi-fold preparation spread. I therefore select the Robustness Adjudicator's S1C41::M-REPEAT as a state-control precursor. I retain the Proposer's minimum-burden tie-break in selecting S1C41 rather than a higher-loading tied candidate.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: S1C41 lies within the stated modifier evidence regions, but no contemporaneous matched E2 reference is included, modifier functionality and true stoichiometry are unverified, and the experiment does not measure 120 C hold drift.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The spread is observed directly in the modified chemistry, so no unmodified-family shape extrapolation is used. Generalization beyond S1C41, the tested preparation protocol, or 80-130 C remains unsupported.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The repeated 80-130 C sweeps directly measure viscosity, but instrument repeatability is not separately quantified in the payload. The 3.40% sweep-fit residual is not treated as preparation-repeat precision.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: This is the targeted uncertainty. Historical E2 preparations showed max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57, including 3.57 at 120 C and 3.34 at 130 C; M-REPEAT estimates the corresponding spread for S1C41 across at least three preparations.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local thermal-response regularities were measured primarily in the original reactive PUR family represented by E1, E2, and E3, with E1 +P retained as a separate chemical-perturbation check; the hold contrast was measured for original E1 and E5. The intended experiment introduces an acrylic-like and/or minor-tackifier-like modifier into the E2-anchored design and therefore does not automatically remain inside the chemistry support of the measured shared thermal-response shape. Direct sweep verification is required unless the audited chemistry-applicability assessment establishes otherwise.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive isothermal viscosity drift during the 120 °C melt-residence window, creating a risk that the adhesive leaves its processing-viscosity window during use.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 hold at 120 °C showed SI_15_60 = 0.5154 and SI_15_90 = 0.9308, corresponding to approximately 52% and 93% viscosity increases. By comparison, E1 showed approximately 9.5% and 16.8% increases over the same intervals.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only two original 120 °C hold trajectories are available, one each for E1 and E5, with four time points from 15 to 90 minutes and no reported independent repeats. In contrast, temperature response was measured over 80–130 °C for multiple E1, E2, and E3 runs. The large difference between the E1 and E5 hold drifts therefore remains poorly mapped across composition and potentially confounded with realization or process history.
measurement_requirements: Use a nonzero modifier loading because the unmodified reactive-core option has no differential prediction and cannot separate the registered level hypotheses.
Measure viscosity directly at 120 and 130 °C and compare the matched-temperature level with the prospectively frozen inert-dilution prediction.

Resolve differences at least beyond the applicable measurement threshold: 3.4% for a direct sweep interpretation, rather than relying on the less discriminating 8.8% one-point reconstruction threshold.
Use an 80–130 °C sweep in 10 °C increments on a freshly prepared sample unless chemistry applicability explicitly validates the shared-shape shortcut for the selected candidate.

Control and fully record preparation, dehydration, thermal history, residence time, and measurement order because E2 showed nominal run max/min ratios of approximately 2.80–3.57 and CV values of approximately 0.46–0.58 across 80–130 °C.
Measure the 120 °C isothermal trajectory at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes with at least two independent repeats and report SI_15_60 without extrapolation.
Include a matched E2 reactive-core reference prepared and measured under the same process history so modifier effects are not conflated with realization-state displacement.
planner.scientific_question: For an E2-anchored formulation containing a nonzero modifier loading, is the directly measured viscosity level at 120–130 °C above, within, or below the inert-dilution prediction, and does that level remain acceptably stable during a matched 120 °C hold? A level above dilution supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, agreement within measurement resolution supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, and a level below dilution supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is resin-modified AC1920+TK100 chemistry, outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was previously measured. Therefore shape transfer cannot be assumed and M-ANCHOR is inadmissible under the binding audit. M-SWEEP is admissible because it measures the processing-window level directly and verifies the thermal-response shape in this chemistry. Its 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like loadings are both inside the externally supported intervention regions, with 5% in the repeatedly documented minor-resin cluster and 15% in the conservative initial acrylic test band.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: A level change within 3.40% of exactly one frozen prediction identifies the corresponding formulation-level model at this composition: -42.76% supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and -72.76% supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. The directly measured 120-130 C level and the newly measured thermal-response shape can then be reported without assuming transfer from unmodified chemistry.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A result at or below -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-ASSOC; a result at or above -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; and a departure from -42.76% exceeding 3.40% falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE. Such rejection supports an alternative only if the result also falls within that alternative's 3.40% acceptance window.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result outside all three 3.40% prediction windows means none of the registered level models adequately describes this composition, even if its direction rejects one or more hypotheses. Given the documented E2 realization variability and the card's moderate process-state risk, process history or preparation-state displacement would remain a plausible ambiguity requiring state-controlled repetition. This sweep does not measure the separate 120 C thermal-hold drift coordinate.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C within the 80-130 C sweep, expressed as the level change relative to the unmodified reactive core; the sweep also yields the fitted apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied and fully supported, but its 17.5% acrylic loading imposes a larger chemistry departure than S1C41 without improving hypothesis-pair separation or measurement interpretability.
Deterministically tied and located at a directly commensurate 20% acrylic evidence anchor, but it uses a higher total modifier burden while providing the same three-pair discrimination as S1C41.
Deterministically tied, but the 22.5% acrylic loading is a larger intervention with no incremental discrimination over the minimum-burden tied card.

Deterministically tied and within the broad supported region, but its 25% acrylic loading is the largest tied perturbation and therefore the greatest departure from the characterized local chemistry without added information value.

It also separates all three hypothesis pairs directly, but its 7.5% tackifier loading lies outside the repeatedly supported 4.8-6.4% cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-SWEEP has the top VOI score of 0.6875 and separates all three registered hypothesis pairs using direct 120-130 C measurements at the more discriminating 3.4% threshold. The binding chemistry audit requires this direct sweep because AC1920+TK100 shape transfer is unverified. Within the genuine five-way tie, S1C41 provides the minimum supported modifier intervention. No registered level hypothesis remains unseparated, although the experiment does not answer the distinct thermal-hold-drift question.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards directly separate all three hypothesis pairs, have identical VOI components, use the chemistry-valid direct sweep, and remain within supported modifier regions. S1C41 is selected because it uses the smallest total modifier burden and smallest departure from the characterized E2 reactive core: 15% acrylic-like plus 5% tackifier-like, versus progressively higher acrylic loadings in the other tied cards. This follows the minimum-sufficient-intervention rule while retaining full two-axis coverage.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed from S1C41::M-SWEEP to S1C41::M-REPEAT. The deterministic score does not adequately encode that one uncontrolled preparation cannot support a 3.40% relative-level classification when the reference chemistry has shown multi-fold between-preparation spread. M-REPEAT retains direct 80-130 C measurements in the modified chemistry while estimating preparation-state variability across at least three realizations. This does not eliminate the need for contemporaneous matched E2 blocks.
residual_decision_risk: S1C41::M-REPEAT still lacks a contemporaneously prepared E2 reactive-core reference, so the modifier-versus-E2 percentage change and registered hypothesis acceptance or falsification criteria remain unattainable from this card alone.
The 3.40% threshold is a fitted-curve residual rather than demonstrated repeat precision for matched S1C41-versus-E2 preparations in AC1920+TK100 chemistry.
The card does not preregister whether 120 C and 130 C are adjudicated separately or combined through a defined estimator.
The dual-axis formulation cannot isolate acrylic-like effects from TK100 effects, total-modifier plasticization, or reactive-core dilution.
Modifier functionality and resulting true NCO:OH stoichiometry remain unverified.
Neither the proposed sweep nor the preferred repeatability card measures the separate 120 C thermal-hold drift coordinate, despite drift being the declared failure mode and least-resolved coordinate.

The binding chemistry audit correctly excludes M-ANCHOR for this modified chemistry. Direct sweeps establish temperature support, but claims of 3.40% classification precision remain unsupported until matched-reference repeatability is measured.
Behavior under weight scalings outside the reported 0.5-1.5 sweep was not evaluated.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: Although S1C41::M-SWEEP is top ranked, its single-preparation protocol cannot directly produce the stated relative observable because it contains no contemporaneous E2 reference. Historical E2 values are unsuitable given max/min ratios of 3.57 at 120 C and 3.34 at 130 C, far exceeding the claimed 3.40% discrimination threshold. All five tied top cards share this defect, so switching among them would not solve it. Among the supplied cards, S1C41::M-REPEAT is the better immediate experiment because it performs 80-130 C sweeps on at least three independent S1C41 preparations and directly quantifies the process-state variability that otherwise makes hypothesis classification uninterpretable. It still does not provide the required matched E2 comparator, so it is a precursor rather than a complete test of the registered relative-level hypotheses. The tied set does not favor a higher-loading candidate: all tied candidates have the same nominal hypothesis coverage, while S1C41 has the smallest modifier burden.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal remains in the unchanged five-card tied top set under every reported single-weight scaling from 0.5 to 1.5. All recommendation_flip_boundary entries are null, top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, and no flipped scenarios were observed. Thus no tested perturbation, defensible or otherwise, changes the deterministic recommendation. The base margin to the first strictly lower card is only 0.002292, and behavior outside the tested scaling range is unknown. This weight robustness cannot repair the protocol-level absence of a matched E2 reference or the mismatch between the 3.40% threshold and observed preparation variability.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The direct 80-130 C sweep appropriately stays within newly measured support for the resin-modified AC1920+TK100 candidate and does not reuse the unmodified shared thermal-response shape outside its validated chemistry domain. M-ANCHOR was correctly excluded by the binding audit. A direct sweep is therefore the right measurement type, but the 3.40% classification threshold still requires validation through matched-reference, independent-preparation repeats in this modified chemistry.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The instrument can directly produce S1C41 viscosities at 120 and 130 C, but the falsification criterion is defined on percentage change relative to E2. Because no matched E2 preparation is included, the protocol as specified cannot directly produce the criterion variable. Importing a historical E2 value would not cure the problem because the documented E2 realization spread greatly exceeds 3.40%. Near the -42.76% boundary, the association and plasticization criteria also lack a resolution margin.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Assignment of the result to any of the three formulation-level hypotheses could instead reflect an unmatched E2 realization-state difference rather than the modifier effect.
objections.objection: The three frozen predictions for S1C41 are numerically well separated: H-LEVEL-DILUTE at -42.76%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC at 17.24%, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC at -72.76%; the smallest pairwise separation is 30.00 percentage points, above the declared 3.40% threshold. However, the proposed M-SWEEP protocol measures only one freshly prepared S1C41 sample and does not include the matched E2 reactive-core reference needed to obtain the stated observable, 'level change relative to the unmodified reactive core.' Therefore the claimed three-way discrimination is only nominal, not delivered by the specified protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment cannot support any conclusion that S1C41 mitigates the stated processing failure mode or remains in its viscosity window during residence time. The proposer does admit this limitation, so it does not create an undeclared entanglement among the registered level hypotheses.
objections.objection: The planner's scientific question asks both whether the 120-130 C level is above, within, or below dilution and whether that level remains stable during a 120 C hold. S1C41::M-SWEEP has no hold times and explicitly does not measure the thermal-hold-drift coordinate, despite excessive hold drift being the declared failure mode and the least-resolved coordinate.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result may distinguish the three frozen aggregate prediction values at this one composition, but it cannot establish which modifier axis caused the deviation or validate an acrylic-association, tackifier-plasticization, or stoichiometric mechanism.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously—15.0% AC1920 and 5.0% TK100—while reducing the reactive-core fraction to 0.80. A single combined formulation cannot isolate acrylic-associated elevation from TK100 effects, total-modifier plasticization, or simple reactive-core dilution. In addition, the local-reactive-core record states that true NCO:OH must be recalculated if a modifier has NCO-reactive functionality, but the proposed protocol contains no material-specification or stoichiometry verification step.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A one-preparation displacement could be misclassified as support for association, dilution, or plasticization, and the nominal 3.40% windows would not represent practical formulation-level resolution.
objections.objection: M-SWEEP specifies min_repeats = 1 and controls_process_state = false, while E2 showed max/min ratios of 3.57 at 120 C and 3.34 at 130 C, with CV values of 0.585 and 0.541. The card itself assigns process_state_risk = 0.75. This observed between-preparation spread is vastly larger than the 3.40% discrimination threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The reported percentage change and hypothesis classification would inherit unregistered reference-selection and aggregation assumptions rather than being a directly measured matched-window comparison.
objections.objection: The absolute S1C41 viscosities at 120 and 130 C are read directly, but the decision observable is a relative change against an unmodified reactive core. The M-SWEEP protocol contains no contemporaneous E2 measurement, so that relative observable requires an unstated historical comparator or imputed reference. The protocol also does not specify whether the two temperatures are adjudicated separately, averaged, or reduced through a fitted level parameter.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The regression residual could be misrepresented as the experimental resolution for a novel-chemistry, between-preparation relative comparison.
objections.objection: The 3.40% threshold is derived from a 1.034x residual of a shared-shape-plus-intercept regression, not from repeat precision for S1C41 versus a matched E2 reference. The fitted E_eta descriptor also inherits the ln(eta) versus 1/T regression assumptions, although the proposer correctly treats the 120 and 130 C viscosity readings themselves as direct.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct level data remain valid, but claims of 3.40% classification precision in the modified family would be unsupported.
objections.objection: The primary 120 and 130 C viscosity readings remain inside the measured support generated by this experiment because M-SWEEP directly measures S1C41 from 80 to 130 C. The proposal does not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared shape to reconstruct the modified candidate, and it correctly rejects M-ANCHOR under the binding audit. The only residual support concern is that the 3.40% discrimination threshold comes from prior fitted-curve residuals rather than demonstrated repeatability in AC1920+TK100 chemistry.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A nominal threshold crossing could be reported as falsification even though the protocol did not directly observe the required relative quantity and cannot resolve near-boundary results reliably.
objections.objection: The stated falsification rules require the measured level change relative to E2 to be compared with -42.76%, but the specified protocol measures no matched E2 reference. A numerical trigger could be produced only by importing an unmatched historical value or adding an unplanned comparator. Moreover, the association and plasticization rules use an exact boundary at -42.76% without a 3.40% uncertainty guard, even though that same resolution is invoked for dilution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A viscosity-level result could be overinterpreted as proof of molecular association or a unique chemical mechanism.
objections.objection: No target validation outcome leakage is evident in the supplied trace. However, rheology alone cannot establish the molecular statement that AC1920 'associates within the melt.' At most, a level above the frozen dilution prediction supports the registered formulation-level association model; the registry itself limits the claim boundary and does not authorize a unique molecular mechanism.

skeptic.recommended_change: Amend S1C41::M-SWEEP to include a contemporaneously prepared E2 reactive-core reference under the same dehydration, preparation, thermal-history, residence-time, and measurement-order conditions; run at least three independent matched preparation blocks; randomize or balance measurement order; and preregister whether 120 and 130 C are adjudicated separately or by a defined combined level estimator. Estimate the modified-versus-E2 uncertainty from those blocks before applying the acceptance windows. If the stated drift failure mode remains part of the decision, also run the available S1C41::M-HOLD-120 protocol with at least two independent repeats. Axis-specific mechanism attribution would additionally require separate acrylic-only and tackifier-only controls from the supplied candidate set.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The primary decision observable is a viscosity change relative to an unmodified E2 reactive core, but S1C41::M-SWEEP specifies only one freshly prepared S1C41 sweep and no matched E2 reference. Given E2 max/min spreads of 3.57 at 120 C and 3.34 at 130 C, an unmatched or historical reference makes the claimed 3.40% three-hypothesis discrimination uninterpretable.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded first to establish the chemistry provenance, same-order comparisons, shared-shape evidence, one-point calibration error, hold contrast, and the status of the separate E1 +P perturbation before any candidate or experiment ranking.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
